FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 31 January 1978, after the draft finalized by the Fruits and Vegetables Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Dehydrated potatoes in different forms are being used in large quantities in the country. The dehydrated potatoes give a consistent taste and flavour, economise on packaging and can help in tiding over the glut period of this perishable commodity, This standard is expected to help in exercising quality control of dehydrated potatoes. 0.3 Dehydrated potatoes are prepared from clean and sound tubers of suitable varieties of potatoes, free frOID blemishes or disease by washing, peeling, trimming and cutting to the required size and shape, blanching, sulphiting and dehydrating under controlled conditions. Processing i. done in a manner which ensures effective preservation of colour, flavour, texture, taste and food value. 0.4 This-standard was first published in 1968. In this revision requirements for total ash and acid insoluble ash have been incorporated and provision for preservatives has been modified. It gives more details of method of test for rehydration ratio and reconstitution and also incorporates Amendment No.1 issued to the standard. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2�1960�. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard .
� Rulca for rounding off numerical values ( "vu,d ).

3

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods otsampling and test for dehydrated potatoes.

2. TERMINOLOGY
2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply.

2.1 RehydratloD Ratio - The ra tio of the mass of the dehydrated material
after cooking and draining of excess water to its mass before cooking.
2~2 Potato Chip. - Strips of potatoes having a thickness between 3 and 6 rnm, obtained by cutting washed, peeled and trimmed potatoes transversely.

2.3 Potato Cube. - Diced, cuboids of 3 to 6 mm dimensions. 2.4 Potato FiDler. - Diced potatoes in the form of fingers having a thickness 3 to 6 mm and length ranging between 25 and 40 mm.

3. TYPES
3.1 Dehydrated potatoes shall be of the following types: a) Chips, b) Fingers, and c) Cubes. 4. REQ,UIREMENTS 4.1 Raw Material. - Dehydrated potatoes shall be prepared from tubers of a suitable variety .of potatoes (Solanum t"b'TOSUm Linn_) harvested at appropriate maturity, The potatoes shall have been properly and fully cured, and shall be free from damage caused by insects, moulds, disease, etc.

4.2 End Product
4.2.1 Dehydrated potatoes shall have a uniform white, golden or yellow colour. They shall have the characteristic odour of potatoes and shall be free from 'scorched, musty or other objectionable odours. 4.2.2 Dehydrated potatoes shall be free from any chemical preservative other than sulphur dioxide, artificial colouring matter, bleaching or flavouring substances. They shall also be free from case hardening. 4.2.3 Dehydrated potatoes shall be free from dust, dirt, stones, lumps of earth or any other extraneous matter. The proportion of blemished pieces bearing eyes, skin or discoloured pieces shall be not more than 1-5 percent by mass.

4

IS I 4626 � 1978

4.2.4 Dehydrated potatoes shall be free from moulds, insect infestation, rodent excreta and other foreign matter.
".2.5 Dehydrated potatoes shall also conform to the requirements given in Table I.

4.2.6 Reconstitution - Dehydrated potatoes shall reconstitute to a good quality product, free front toughness or mushiness having a characterisuc taste, colour and odour of cooked potatoes, when one part by mass of the dehydrated potatoes arc cooked (sirnmcreu ) in 15 parts by m..1SS of the one percent sodium chloride solution for 30 minutes. The time taken for cooking shall be ..the time from the start of boiling ( simmer iug ).
5. PACKING AND MARKING

5.1 Packing - Dehydrated potatoes shall be packed in clean, sound. moistureproof containers made of tin-plate, laminated foils or "lilY suitable material which would prevent the uptake of moisture,
5.2 Marking - Each container shall be marked or labelled with the following particulars: a) Name and type of the material, b) Name and address of the manufacturer, c) Net mass, d) Declaration to the effect that permitted preservatives have been used, e) Batch or code number indicating the date ormanufacture, and f) Manufacturer's licence number.

5

IS : 4626. 1978
5.3 DIS Certification Marking

The product may also be marked with Standard Mark.
5.3.t The use of the Standard Mark is governed by tbe provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. Tbe details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from tbe Bureau of Indian Standards.

6. SAMPLING
6.1 Representative samples of the material for testing conformity to this specification shall be drawn according to the method given in Appendix G of IS: 4624-1978-.

7. TESTS
7.1 Tests shall be carried out as prescribed in the relevant appendices specified in col 4 and 5 of Table 1.

APPENDIX
DETER~IINATION

A

[ Table I, ltem (iv) ]
OF REHYDRATION RATIO
A-I. PROCEDURE
,A-I.I Cook ( sirnmer ) in a beaker one part by mass of dehydrated potatoes in fifteen parts by mass of one percent sodium chloride solution for 30 minutes and then allow them to cool at room temperature for 45 minutes. The time taken for cooking shall be the time taken from tbe start of boiling (simmering). Drain off excess solution by covering the beaker with watch glass with convex surface and inverting the container for five minutes. Weigh cooled material.

A-2. CALCULATION
A-2.1 Rehydration Ratio == MR : MD where ,,\{R == mass of reconstituted dehydrated potatoes. and MD = mass of dehydrated material before cooking.
